name: Taiwan High Speed Rail 700T
description: The 700T adapted Japan’s Series 700 as a 12-car high-speed train for Taiwan’s route, environment, regulation and operating needs.

places.note: Taiwan is the operating region. The manufacturer unveiled the train in Japan.

date.label: 30 January 2004
date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: Taiwan High Speed Rail Corporation and its Japanese suppliers unveiled the 700T at Kawasaki’s Hyogo Works in Japan.

evidence.supports: The manufacturer dates and locates the unveiling.

date.label: 5 January 2007
date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: Taiwan High Speed Rail began passenger service with its 700T fleet between Banqiao and Zuoying.

evidence.locator: Operational Highlights, High Speed Rail Service
evidence.supports: The operator dates the first revenue runs and gives the section.

evidence.locator: High-speed railway route and stations; Rolling-stock specifications
evidence.supports: The bureau confirms opening date, stations and the model adopted.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated milestone retained here for this design or deployment.

community_entry.rationale: Taiwan High Speed Rail began passenger service with its 700T fleet between Banqiao and Zuoying.

links.statement: Taiwan’s high-speed rail operator received trains developed from the Japanese Series 700 design. The Japanese manufacturers adapted the model for Taiwan's route, conditions and requirements.

evidence.supports: A manufacturer names Series 700 as the basis and details local adaptation.
The Railway Bureau confirms adoption of the locally adapted Series 700 derivative.
